text:
maria: Drafting the release note for the Adaptive routing beta. Need a short whats-new line, a canary rollout note (10% then 50%), a tiny migration tip, and two SDK examples (curl + go). I'll open a docs PR in ~20m. ping @oliver @sasha

oliver: Good. Call out the config key explicitly (adaptive_routing.enabled). Also list fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated -> fallback-variant). Ops needs the rollout percentages and canary duration.

sasha: I'll take SDK snippets. Will do a curl example for changelog and a Go example for the how-to. Will keep both <10 lines.

ben: QA: add a Known issues bullet with repro steps and a staging link. Also please add a one-line changelog entry for the feed (short).

emily: Migration note: teams using route-level caching should be warned about KV cache warmups; maybe recommend a graceful ramp or pin variant. I can draft that paragraph.

docs-ci: PR #4890 1: staging linkcheck: 404s: [/tutorials/old-routing-guide], lint: 1 long line in docs/adaptive-routing.md. Preview: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/adaptive-routing/preview-4890

maria: Thanks. I'll add redirect from /tutorials/old-routing-guide -> /docs/adaptive-routing/migrate and fix the long line. Draft blurb (copy-edit welcome):

maria: ```
What's new: Adaptive routing (beta)
- Adaptive routing automatically prefers cost-efficient model variants and falls back to higher-tier variants when needed. Opt-in per route via adaptive_routing.enabled = true.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic for 24h, then 50% for 48h before global rollout.
Known issues:
- On some T4 hosts, sequence length 512 can see a transient ~5-12ms latency increase while KV cache warms. Mitigation: pin variant or disable adaptive_routing for latency-critical routes. Repro: ssh to staging and run ./tools/bench --seq 512 --target routing-canary.
Migration note:
- If you have route-level caching, expect a short warmup; consider a slow rollout or pre-warm requests.

Quick examples:
Curl (changelog-friendly):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rodeo-3","prompt":"Write a haiku","routing":{"adaptive_routing":{"enabled":true}}}'

Go (how-to):
```go
import "github.com/redwood/inference-go"
client := inference.NewClient(nil)
resp, _ := client.Generate(context.Background(), 
  inference.Request{Model: "rodeo-3", Prompt: "Summarize", Routing: map[string]any{"adaptive_routing": map[string]bool{"enabled": true}}})
fmt.Println(resp.Text)
```
```

sasha: Curl looks good. I'll shorten the Go example to remove error handling and use a compact struct. Also will add a tiny streaming pointer for SDKs.

oliver: Suggest phrasing change: replace 'falls back to higher-tier variants' with 'automatically falls back to compatible variants' and expand fallback chain to 'hosted -> dedicated -> fallback-variant (configurable)'.

maria: updated in PR, added redirect and staging preview link: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/adaptive-routing/preview-4890

docs-ci: Linkcheck (preview-4890): 0 404s, 0 lint errors, 1 warning (long line trimmed). Full report: https://ci.redwood.ai/reports/4890/linkcheck

ben: I'll add the one-line changelog entry after merge. Can someone watch the release-index rendering?

emily: I'll post a short migration note in the migration guide and ping customers with dedicated capacity who have route-level caching.

sasha: Watching the index render, will adjust snippet escaping if needed.

maria: Merging now. If anything breaks we will revert and publish rollback notes. Thanks all :rocket:
